name: WE Energies

profile.address: Pewaukee Data Center, W237N1500, Busse Road, RidgeView Corporate Park, City of Pewaukee, Waukesha County, Wisconsin, 53188
profile.reading:
In the RidgeView Corporate Park business park in the City of Pewaukee, Waukesha County, Wisconsin, We Energies operates a facility identified as the Pewaukee Data Center at W237N1500 Busse Road. We Energies is the trade name of Wisconsin Electric Power Company, one of the two principal utility subsidiaries of Milwaukee based WEC Energy Group, and it is one of the larger investor owned utilities in the Upper Midwest, serving more than 1.1 million electric customers and roughly the same number of natural gas customers across Wisconsin, plus electric service in Michigan's Upper Peninsula and steam service to downtown Milwaukee.

A utility of that size runs a substantial amount of internal computing infrastructure that rarely gets public attention because none of it is offered commercially. Grid operations alone require systems for supervisory control and data acquisition, outage management, and increasingly for the kind of real time monitoring that smart meters and distribution automation depend on. On top of that sits the ordinary corporate technology load of a company with over a million customer accounts: billing systems, customer information systems, and the back office applications any utility of this scale needs to run continuously. Pewaukee, a western Milwaukee suburb with easy highway access via I-94, is a plausible and unremarkable location for a utility to place enterprise IT capacity, whether as a primary site or as a backup facility for its core operations closer to downtown Milwaukee.

We Energies has not published a page describing this specific building, its square footage, its power capacity, or what systems it houses, and no news coverage identifying it as a named, standalone facility has surfaced. That is ordinary for a utility's internal data center. Unlike a colocation provider, We Energies has no commercial reason to publish capacity or design details for a building that exists purely to support the company's own grid operations and back office systems, and utilities generally treat the physical security and specifications of facilities tied to grid control functions as sensitive rather than promotional information. What can be said with confidence is the location, the parent company, and the type of institution behind it. Beyond that, the building's role in We Energies' broader operations, and any details about its scale, remain undisclosed.

reading:
We Energies is the trade name of Wisconsin Electric Power Company and Wisconsin Gas LLC, both subsidiaries of Milwaukee based WEC Energy Group. It appears in this registry as an enterprise private operator, meaning the facility recorded here is a building the utility runs for itself rather than one it leases to tenants. By the company's own published key facts, We Energies served 1,185,000 electric customers as of December 2025, about 1,190,000 natural gas customers and 369 steam customers, with 2,916 active regular employees as of February 2026, across southeastern Wisconsin and Michigan's Upper Peninsula.

The registry facility carries a precise address, the Pewaukee Data Center at W237N1500 Busse Road in the RidgeView Corporate Park in the City of Pewaukee, Waukesha County. Beyond that address, the public record is genuinely thin, and it is worth being exact about how thin. We Energies publishes no page describing this building, no floor area, no capacity figure of any kind, and no statement of what it contains. No city of Pewaukee or Waukesha County document describing it was located in this research, and no state filing naming it was found. A utility of this size plainly runs substantial internal computing for grid control, metering, billing and corporate systems, but that is an inference about what utilities do, not a fact established about this address, and this registry records no capacity and makes no claim about the building's size or function beyond its name in the source data.

What is heavily documented is We Energies in the other role that puts utilities next to this industry, as the supplier that data centers depend on. The Public Service Commission of Wisconsin approved a modified very large customer tariff for the utility on April 24, 2026. We Energies had proposed ten year agreements applying at a 500 megawatt threshold with an optional capacity only subscription. The commission lengthened the minimum term to fifteen years to limit cost shifting, lowered the threshold to 100 megawatts to align it with the level at which new generation requires commission approval, and removed the capacity only option so that the subscription is mandatory for eligible customers, with commissioners stating that existing Wisconsin customers should not subsidize service to data centers. Projects in the utility's territory named in that proceeding include Microsoft at Mount Pleasant and a large campus at Port Washington, and the commission's record notes that data center load could roughly double We Energies demand by 2030. That regulatory record is about power sold to others, not about the Pewaukee building, and the two should not be conflated.
